_comment: In-context grid generation. Per mesh we run the full n_context x n_ic grid: n_context hidden-physics draws (each a SYSTEM to infer) x n_ic shared freestream/IC draws. A column (fixed physics AND fixed save_t, varying IC) is one multi-IC system for the demonstration regime; a row (fixed IC, varying physics) is the SAME starting frame under many contexts, which forces the model to use the context instead of memorising frame appearance. context_param_specs + save_t -> params.json (the system, and what is inferred); ic_param_specs -> ic.json (shared across contexts). STANDARDISED with the other generator in this directory: both draw the SAME hidden-physics and freestream specs, both draw a per-system frame interval from the SAME save_t_spec, both write that interval into params.json, and both size a run by a frame COUNT rather than an iteration cap. That is what makes the two corpora interchangeable for context-switch training -- a run means the same thing to hfm/data.py whichever generator produced it. Keep the specs below in sync when either is edited.
_save_t_note: Drawn once per CONTEXT (so params.json is identical down a grid column and the column still groups into one system) and written into params.json. A single fixed interval would give the dt probe a constant target -- hfm/data.py warns 'constant -- dt probe target is degenerate' -- and, because it is the presence of save_t in params.json that flips a run from 'legacy' to 'has_save_t' in the loader, a corpus without it trains under stride augmentation on an inferred dt instead of stride 1 on a recorded one.
_steps_note: Frames per run, mirroring gen_alternating's steps_per_segment: end_t = steps_per_run * save_t, so every run yields exactly steps_per_run + 1 frames whatever its interval. The old n_iter cap made run length depend on the adaptive step, i.e. on the physics draw, so viscous runs came out shorter than inviscid ones.
_context_note: Hidden physics — NOT visible in a single frame, so the model must infer them from transitions. These define the system and go in params.json. C_v lives here (constant per system) because the data loader reads it from params.json to convert primitives->conserved; it mildly affects the initial energy channel, so move it to ic_param_specs for a perfectly-shared conserved start frame at the cost of not inferring it.
_ic_note: Freestream / boundary conditions that DEFINE the initial condition (and are largely visible in the frame). Shared across all contexts within a mesh, so the same starting frames recur under every physics draw.
_nozzle_note: nozzle removed: its geometry is two OPEN wall polylines, which the gmsh-based create_mesh (closed curve loops) cannot mesh — every nozzle draw fails deterministically on all platforms and only wastes retries. Re-add once create_mesh supports open chains (e.g. gmsh OCC fragment).
